controls.statement: Backup restoration has not been demonstrated within the required recovery objectives.
controls.primary_reason: Approved recovery objectives and protected-data scope provide fixed policy inputs, and authenticated restore results can be compared directly with those limits.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved recovery record defines the protected data scope and numeric recovery objectives for the assessed release.
Current authenticated restore-test evidence covers the complete protected scope and meets every approved recovery objective.

controls.statement: The release cannot meet its approved reliability objectives under expected operating conditions.
controls.primary_reason: The control explicitly uses approved reliability objectives, so fixed observations for the approved operating profile can be compared to their exact thresholds.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A versioned approved policy defines numeric reliability objectives and the operating conditions for the assessed release.
Current execution or environment evidence for the approved operating conditions meets every bound reliability objective.

controls.statement: The production artifact cannot be traced to reviewed source, dependencies, build process, tests, and approval.
controls.primary_reason: Content-addressed provenance, dependency records, build attestations, test results, and approval records can form a complete fixed trace for the exact artifact.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The production artifact digest is bound by verified provenance to the exact reviewed source and build process.
The verified build record includes the complete dependency inventory used to create the production artifact.
Current test and approval records identify the same source, build, and production artifact digests.

controls.statement: A release blocker has been relabeled, suppressed, or accepted without an accountable risk owner.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned gate policy defines release blockers, and authenticated history and ownership records can show every relabel, suppression, or acceptance and its owner.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every blocker defined by the versioned release policy retains an authenticated status-change and exception history.
Each relabeled, suppressed, or accepted blocker has an active accountable risk-owner identity in the approved ownership record.

controls.primary_reason: A release ledger can deterministically require a nonempty identifier and prove its uniqueness within the declared project release namespace.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record has a nonempty identifier that occurs exactly once in the declared project release namespace.

controls.statement: Record the exact source commit or commits.
controls.primary_reason: Source identities are immutable machine values, and the recorded set can be compared exactly with the source inputs in verified build provenance.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record contains one or more syntactically valid immutable source commit identifiers.
The recorded source commit set exactly equals the source commit set in verified provenance for every release artifact.

controls.statement: Record the immutable application artifact digest.
controls.primary_reason: The recorded digest can be parsed with a fixed algorithm and compared byte-for-byte with a fresh digest of the exact application artifact.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record contains an approved cryptographic digest algorithm and digest that match the exact application artifact bytes.

controls.statement: Record every deployable service, worker, scheduled job, frontend bundle, and infrastructure component included.
controls.primary_reason: Deployable release contents are finite and can be enumerated from sealed build and deployment manifests, then compared with the release component record.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Sealed build and deployment manifests produce a complete inventory of deployable components included in the release.
The release record lists exactly every component in the complete deployable inventory with its type and immutable identity.

controls.statement: Record database schema and migration versions.
controls.primary_reason: Database schema and migration identifiers are structured machine values that can be collected from the target environment and matched to the release record.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A read-only environment query returns the schema and migration version for every database in the approved release scope.
The release record exactly matches every collected database schema and migration version.

controls.primary_reason: Versioned production configuration identities can be collected through read-only connectors and compared exactly with their release-recorded values.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Read-only environment evidence identifies every versioned production configuration in the approved release scope.
The release record exactly lists the collected production configuration identities and versions.

controls.statement: Record feature flags and their intended launch states.
controls.primary_reason: Feature-flag inventories and intended states are finite structured data, so complete environment and release records can be compared without interpretation.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A read-only flag-system query produces the complete feature-flag inventory for the approved launch scope.
The release record lists every inventoried flag and one explicit intended launch state for each flag.

controls.statement: Record the intended production regions, accounts, projects, clusters, and domains.
controls.primary_reason: The intended deployment scope is a release-owner declaration, and a schema can require explicit identifiers for each applicable location and resource type.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated release record contains explicit production region, account, project, cluster, and domain lists, including recorded empty or not-applicable states where permitted.

controls.statement: Record the target deployment date and change window.
controls.primary_reason: Deployment date and change-window boundaries are structured time values whose presence, ordering, timezone, and release binding are objectively validatable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record contains a valid target deployment time and ordered change-window start and end timestamps with an explicit timezone.

controls.statement: Freeze or formally track changes after the readiness evidence snapshot.
controls.primary_reason: Content-addressed snapshots and authenticated change history can prove whether every later change was prevented or formally recorded after the evidence cutoff.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The readiness evidence record identifies an immutable source, artifact, configuration, and policy snapshot with a cutoff time.
Every change after the cutoff is either rejected by the freeze policy or present in the authenticated change-tracking record.

controls.statement: List supported countries, languages, currencies, time zones, browsers, devices, and accessibility targets.
controls.primary_reason: These are intended support-policy dimensions, so the authenticated release scope is authoritative and can require explicit typed lists or recorded non-applicability.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved support-scope record explicitly lists countries, languages, currencies, time zones, browsers, devices, and accessibility targets or a justified not-applicable value for each dimension.
